paper_metadata.title: Microstructure, oxidation resistance and high-temperature strength of γ' hardened Pt-base alloys

evidence.quote: Starting from the base composition with 12 at.% Al, 6 at.% Cr, 5 at.% Ni and Pt balance, precipitation hardened Pt-Al-Cr-Ni alloys with additions of 2 at.% Mo, Re, Ru and W, respectively, were investigated.
As benchmark in terms of strength, the Ni-base superalloy CMSX-4 was used.
Mo, Re and W additions lead to a measurable increase of the g0 fraction in g0 precipitation hardened Pt-base alloys.
Alloy Pt77Al12Cr6Ni5 shows a dense corundum scale after ageing in air, also with additions of 2 at.% Mo, Re and Ru, pointing at a good oxidation resistance.

Pt80Al11Cr3Ni6 was heat treated for 12 h at 1500°C and subsequently water quenched, leading to a single-phase g microstructure.
Pt78.5Al12.5Cr3Ni6 was also homogenized for 12 h at 1500°C but subsequently air cooling results in the precipitation of 300 nm sized g0 cubes.
It was not possible to achieve a single-phase g matrix in the ﬁve-component alloys by a homogenization heat treatment at 1510 /C14 C.
